next_candidate.rationale: Different model family. 12B parameters with QAT Q4 quantization. Tests whether a genuinely different architecture can pass the policy gate.

key_finding: Both Liquid LFM2.5 models (2.6B and 8B-A1B) fail the policy gate. The 8B model is NOT better than the 2.6B — it's worse (55% vs 65%). This suggests the Liquid model family has a systematic weakness in the DEFER/RETRIEVE action distinctions required by the DAPH controller, regardless of capacity.
scientific_interpretation: Increasing model capacity within the Liquid LFM2.5 family does NOT fix the policy interface problem. The 8B-A1B (Mixture-of-Experts, 1B active) actually performs worse than the 2.6B dense model. This is evidence that the bottleneck is not raw capacity but model-family-specific understanding of the action semantics, particularly DEFER vs STOP.
